chunks: With the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ibn Faddhal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah or from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon them both, the blessings of God and His mercy, from Jabir ibn Abdillah who said: the Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said to us:

Cover your vessels, tie shut your water-skins, close your doors, and keep your livestock and your families indoors from the time the sun sets until the darkness of nightfall passes. Indeed, the devils cannot uncover a lid nor untie a fastening. And indeed, the devils are dispatched from the time the sun sets. And extinguish your lamps, for the little vermin [mouse] can set the house ablaze upon its inhabitants.

key_terms.أَجِيفُوا: Close/shut (your doors) -- imperative of ajafa, to push a door closed
key_terms.أَوْكُوا: Tie shut (your water-skins) -- imperative of awka, to fasten or seal a water-skin by tying its mouth
key_terms.الْفُوَيْسِقَةَ: The little vermin (mouse/rat) -- diminutive of faasiqa, a prophetic designation for the mouse
key_terms.تُضْرِمُ: Sets ablaze/kindles -- from adh-rama, describing how a mouse drags a lamp wick and ignites the house
key_terms.خَمِّرُوا: Cover (your vessels) -- imperative form of khamara, to cover or conceal food containers
key_terms.فَحْمَةُ الْعِشَاءِ: The darkness of nightfall -- the intense darkness immediately after sunset
key_terms.وِكَاءً: A fastening/cord used to seal the mouth of a water-skin

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad teach about protecting the home from devils and fire at nightfall?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad instructs the believers through his companion Jabir ibn Abdillah to take specific protective precautions during the twilight period between sunset and nightfall. He commands them to cover food vessels, fasten water-skins, shut doors, and bring livestock and family members inside. The reason given is that devils are unleashed at sunset and possess certain physical limitations -- they cannot open sealed containers or unfasten knots. The Prophet also warns about extinguishing oil lamps at night, as a small mouse dragging a wick could burn down an entire house. These instructions reflect practical household safety combined with spiritual awareness of unseen dangers during the transitional period of dusk. The original audience of early Muslim society would have understood 'al-fuwaysiqa' (the little vermin) as a well-known prophetic designation for the mouse, classified among the five harmful creatures that may be killed even in sacred precincts.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 18. And with the preceding chain of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ibn Faddhal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah or Abu Ja’far, peace be upon them both, from Jabir ibn Abdillah that: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said to us:

"Cover your utensils and put a lid over the vessels from which you drink, and shut your doors tight, and tie down your herds, and send your family members indoors, as the sun sets till when the darkness of Isha is dispelled. Surely, the devils do not open the covers, nor do they undo the lids. And the devils are sent off when the sun sets. And put off your lamps, for sometimes the rats kindle fire from it setting the whole house on fire, on its inmates."
